questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, which sanctions-related instruments must the bank take into account when following the Government's orders under section 51A of the UAPA and section 12A of the WMD Act?
questions.answer: The bank must take into account other UNSCRs and the lists in the First and Fourth Schedules of the UAPA, 1967, including any amendments, for compliance with those Government orders.
questions.evidence:
the bank shall take into account:
(1) other UNSCRs and
(2) lists in the first schedule and the fourth schedule of UAPA, 1967 and any amendments to the same for compliance with the Government orders on implementation of section 51A of the UAPA and section 12A of the WMD Act.

questions.question: Must a commercial bank account for amendments to the UAPA, 1967 when considering the First and Fourth Schedule lists for compliance with the Government's orders?
questions.answer: Yes. The bank must take into account any amendments to the UAPA, 1967 when ensuring compliance with the Government orders implementing section 51A of the UAPA and section 12A of the WMD Act.
questions.evidence: lists in the first schedule and the fourth schedule of UAPA, 1967 and any amendments to the same for compliance with the Government orders on implementation of section 51A of the UAPA and section 12A of the WMD Act.

unanswerable.question: How many days does a commercial bank have after a new UNSCR or an amendment to the UAPA schedules is notified before it must incorporate the change into its compliance framework?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the bank to take these instruments into account but does not state any notification, implementation, or review deadline.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what does the RBI require regarding the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 and the rules made under it?
questions.answer: The bank must ensure adherence to the Act’s provisions and the Rules made thereunder.
questions.evidence: The bank shall ensure adherence to the provisions of Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, and Rules made thereunder.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what further compliance is required when the RBI issues instructions concerning the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010?
questions.answer: The bank must comply with any instructions or communications on the matter issued by the RBI from time to time, based on advice received from the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
questions.evidence: Further, the bank shall also ensure meticulous compliance with any instructions / communications on the matter issued from time to time by the RBI based on advice received from the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.

unanswerable.question: What deadline must a commercial bank meet for reporting its compliance with the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 to the RBI?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires adherence to the Act, Rules made thereunder, and relevant RBI instructions, but it does not specify any reporting requirement or deadline.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, how often must its money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment be reviewed?
questions.answer: The Board, or a Board committee to which it has delegated this power, determines the assessment’s frequency based on the assessment’s outcome, but the bank must review it at least annually.
questions.evidence: Further, the Board or a committee of the Board to which it has delegated power shall determine the periodicity of the risk assessment exercise, in alignment with the outcome of the risk assessment exercise. However, the bank shall review it at least annually.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, where must the results of our money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment be reported?
questions.answer: The results must be presented to the Board or the Board committee that has been delegated this responsibility. They must also be made available to competent authorities and self-regulating bodies.
questions.evidence: The bank shall present the outcome of the exercise to the Board or any committee of the Board to which power has been delegated in this regard. The outcome shall also be made available to competent authorities and self-regulating bodies.

unanswerable.question: How many days does a commercial bank have after completing its money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment to present the results to the Board?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the outcome to be presented to the Board or a delegated Board committee, but it specifies no deadline in days for doing so.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what must we do when an existing customer has not submitted a PAN, an equivalent e-document, or Form No. 60 by the date notified by the Central Government?
questions.answer: The bank must temporarily cease operations in the account until the customer submits one of those documents. Before doing so, it must give the customer an accessible notice and a reasonable opportunity to be heard.
questions.evidence: failing which the bank shall temporarily cease operations in the account until the customer submits the PAN or equivalent e-documents thereof or Form No. 60. Provided that before temporarily ceasing operations for an account, the bank shall give the customer an accessible notice and a reasonable opportunity to be heard.

questions.question: For a commercial bank's existing customer's loan account, what is permitted if the bank temporarily ceases operations because the PAN or Form No. 60 requirement has not been met?
questions.answer: Only credits are allowed in the loan account. For asset accounts such as loan accounts, temporary ceasing of operations means that only credits may be made.
questions.evidence: In case of asset accounts such as loan accounts, for the purpose of ceasing the operation in the account, only credits shall be allowed.

unanswerable.question: What maximum grace period, in days, may a commercial bank allow an existing customer to submit a PAN or Form No. 60 after the Central Government's notified deadline?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any number of days or grace period; it only refers to the date that the Central Government may notify.

questions.question: For a commercial bank that offers at-par cheque facilities to co-operative banks, what monitoring and risk review must it undertake?
questions.answer: It must monitor the at-par cheque facility and review the arrangements to assess the credit and reputational risks arising from them.
questions.evidence: The ‘at par’ cheque facility offered by the bank to co-operative banks shall be monitored and such arrangements be reviewed to assess the risks including credit risk and reputational risk arising therefrom.

questions.question: For a commercial bank that offers at-par cheque facilities to co-operative banks, what record-verification right must it retain?
questions.answer: It must retain the right to verify the customer co-operative banks’ or societies’ records for compliance with the applicable KYC and AML instructions.
questions.evidence: The right to verify the records maintained by the customer cooperative banks / societies for compliance with the extant instructions on KYC and AML under such arrangements shall be retained by bank.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a commercial bank review the risks arising from its at-par cheque facility arrangements with co-operative banks?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires monitoring and review of the arrangements but does not specify a review frequency, interval, or deadline.

questions.question: For a remittance of ₹50,000 or more, how must a commercial bank fund a demand draft, transfer, or traveller’s cheque?
questions.answer: It must debit the customer’s account or use the customer’s cheques; cash payment is not permitted for the transaction.
questions.evidence: (1) Any remittance of funds by way of demand draft, mail / telegraphic transfer / NEFT / IMPS or any other mode and issue of travellers’ cheques for value of ₹50,000 and above shall be effected by debit to the customer’s account or against cheques and not against cash payment.

questions.question: When must a commercial bank include the purchaser’s name on a demand draft, pay order, or banker’s cheque?
questions.answer: The issuing bank must include the purchaser’s name on the face of the instrument for instruments issued on or after September 15, 2018.
questions.evidence: Further, the bank shall incorporate the name of the purchaser on the face of the demand draft, pay order, banker’s cheque, etc., by the issuing bank. These instructions shall take effect for such instruments issued on or after September 15, 2018.

unanswerable.question: What monetary penalty does a commercial bank incur if it issues a demand draft without the purchaser’s name on its face?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the purchaser’s name to be included and specifies an effective date, but it does not state any penalty for non-compliance.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what due diligence must we apply to clients and transactions connected to countries that FATF says do not apply its recommendations adequately?
questions.answer: We must apply enhanced due diligence that is effective and proportionate to the risks for business relationships and transactions involving natural and legal persons, including financial institutions, from those countries. We must also give special attention to such relationships and transactions.
questions.evidence: The bank shall apply enhanced due diligence measures, which are effective and proportionate to the risks, to business relationships and transactions with natural and legal persons (including financial institutions) from countries for which this is called for by the FATF.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, what must we examine and retain for transactions involving customers from FATF-listed jurisdictions, and when must we provide the records to regulators?
questions.answer: We must examine the background and purpose of the transactions, retain written findings together with all documents, and make them available to the RBI or other relevant authorities upon request.
questions.evidence: The bank shall examine the background and purpose of transactions with persons (including legal persons and other financial institutions) from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements and countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations, retain written findings together with all documents, and make them available to the RBI / other relevant authorities, on request.

unanswerable.question: As a commercial bank, how many days must we retain written findings and supporting documents for transactions involving customers from FATF-listed jurisdictions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires retaining written findings and documents and making them available to authorities on request, but it does not specify any retention period or number of days.

questions.question: Under the general restriction, for whom must a commercial bank collect an account payee cheque?
questions.answer: Only for the payee constituent. A commercial bank must not collect an account payee cheque for any other person.
questions.evidence: The bank shall not collect account payee cheques for any person other than the payee constituent.

questions.question: For a co-operative credit society customer of a commercial bank, what cheque-value limit applies when the bank elects to collect an account payee cheque, and what membership condition must the payee meet?
questions.answer: The cheque amount must not exceed ₹50,000, and the named payee must be a constituent of the co-operative credit society whose account is credited.
questions.evidence: The bank shall, at its option, collect account payee cheques drawn for an amount not exceeding ₹50,000 to the account of its customers who are co-operative credit societies, provided the payees of such cheques are the constituents of such co-operative credit societies.

unanswerable.question: Must a commercial bank obtain prior approval from the co-operative credit society before collecting an account payee cheque of ₹50,000 or less?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits collection at the bank's option subject to the amount limit and the payee's constituent status, but it does not state any requirement for prior approval from the society.

questions.question: Under the RBI Commercial Banks (KYC) Directions, 2025, when must a commercial bank implement countermeasures requested by an international or intergovernmental organisation?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must implement countermeasures when called upon to do so by an international or intergovernmental organisation of which India is a member and which is accepted by the Central Government.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake countermeasures when called upon so to do by any international or intergovernmental organisation of which India is a member and which is accepted by the Central Government.

questions.question: Under the RBI Commercial Banks (KYC) Directions, 2025, what conditions must an international or intergovernmental organisation meet before a commercial bank is required to act on its request for countermeasures?
questions.answer: India must be a member of the organisation, and the organisation must be accepted by the Central Government.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake countermeasures when called upon so to do by any international or intergovernmental organisation of which India is a member and which is accepted by the Central Government.

unanswerable.question: Under the RBI Commercial Banks (KYC) Directions, 2025, within how many days must a commercial bank begin implementing countermeasures after an accepted international or intergovernmental organisation calls upon it to do so?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the bank to undertake countermeasures when called upon, but it specifies no deadline or time period for implementation.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, do the RBI's KYC requirements replace its obligations under other laws and regulations, or do they operate in addition to them?
questions.answer: They operate in addition to other laws, rules, regulations, and directions in force; they do not displace or derogate from those obligations.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

questions.question: When implementing the RBI's KYC requirements, must a commercial bank continue to comply with other regulatory directions that remain in force?
questions.answer: Yes. The RBI KYC requirements are cumulative, so complying with them does not remove the bank's obligations under other directions in force.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

unanswerable.question: If the RBI's KYC requirements for a commercial bank conflict with another law or regulation, which requirement must the bank follow?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that the KYC requirements are cumulative and do not derogate from other requirements, but it provides no rule for resolving conflicts or stating which requirement prevails.

questions.question: At a commercial bank, when using the video customer identification process (V-CIP) for CDD of a proprietorship firm, what extra document must we obtain besides identifying the proprietor?
questions.answer: We must also obtain the equivalent electronic document containing the proprietorship firm’s activity proofs, as referred to in paragraphs 31 and 32, in addition to completing CDD of the proprietor.
questions.evidence: Provided that in case of CDD of a proprietorship firm, the bank shall also obtain the equivalent e-document of the activity proofs with respect to the proprietorship firm, as mentioned in paragraph 31 and paragraph 32, apart from undertaking CDD of the proprietor.

questions.question: At a commercial bank, can the video customer identification process (V-CIP) be used to convert an existing account opened in non-face-to-face mode using Aadhaar OTP e-KYC, and to update KYC for eligible customers?
questions.answer: Yes. A commercial bank may use V-CIP both to convert such existing accounts and to carry out KYC updates or periodic KYC updates for eligible customers.
questions.evidence: (2) Conversion of existing accounts opened in non-face-to-face mode using Aadhaar OTP based e-KYC authentication as per paragraph 25. (3) Updation / Periodic updation of KYC for eligible customers.

unanswerable.question: At a commercial bank, within how many days must V-CIP be completed after onboarding a new individual customer?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 26 permits V-CIP for CDD during new individual-customer onboarding but specifies no deadline or number of days for completing it.

questions.question: Under the RBI's KYC Directions for commercial banks, what must a bank do to keep monitoring its customers after onboarding?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must carry out ongoing due diligence of its customers, checking that customer transactions remain consistent with what the bank knows about the customer, the customer's business and risk profile, and the source of funds or wealth.
questions.evidence: The bank shall undertake ongoing due diligence of customers to ensure that their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers’ business and risk profile, the source of funds / wealth.

questions.question: When a commercial bank performs ongoing due diligence, what customer-related factors must it use to judge whether the transactions are appropriate?
questions.answer: It must assess whether the transactions match the bank's knowledge about the customer, the customer's business and risk profile, and the source of funds or wealth.
questions.evidence: ensure that their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers’ business and risk profile, the source of funds / wealth

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a commercial bank conduct ongoing due diligence on its customers under the RBI KYC Directions, 2025?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires ongoing due diligence but does not state any review frequency, interval, or deadline for performing it.

questions.question: For a sole proprietorship customer, how many documents proving the firm's business activity must a commercial bank collect?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must obtain any two of the specified documents (or their equivalent e-documents) as proof of business or activity in the name of the proprietary firm.
questions.evidence: the bank shall also obtain any two of the following documents or the equivalent e-documents thereof as proof of business / activity in the name of the proprietary firm

questions.question: What kinds of documents can a commercial bank accept as proof of business activity for a sole proprietorship?
questions.answer: Acceptable documents include a government registration certificate (including an Udyam Registration Certificate), a municipal Shop and Establishment certificate or licence, sales and income tax returns, a CST/VAT/GST certificate, and other documents listed in the Directions.
questions.evidence: (1) Registration certificate including Udyam Registration Certificate (URC) issued by the Government. (2) Certificate / licence issued by the municipal authorities under Shop and Establishment Act (3) Sales and income tax returns (4) CST / VAT / GST certificate

unanswerable.question: Within what period must a commercial bank obtain the two proof-of-business documents when onboarding a sole proprietorship customer?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies how many documents are required and the types of documents acceptable, but it states no timeframe or deadline for obtaining them.
